summary: The changes close several previously identified holes, but the enforcement chain still has multiple independently exploitable trust-boundary failures. Most seriously, mutable control-plane files can be changed by lower-trust worktree workers, Python startup imports can shadow the enforcement dependencies before the new bytecode protections activate, and the authority-to-merge interval is vulnerable to post-verification mutation and pruned-but-unmerged work. I found no concrete Bash 3.2 or Python 3.9 incompatibility, and the supplied artifact contains no task partition whose globs can overlap.

findings.claim: A lower-trust worktree worker can rewrite the unsealed manifest outside its measured worktree, widen its own lane, and have both gates accept and merge the out-of-lane patch.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:42 explicitly says Antigravity/Cursor lack out-of-worktree confinement. `cmd_gate_receipt` rereads the mutable manifest and derives `allow` from it at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:2351-2359 and :2409. The authority independently rereads that same file at scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py:917-920 and uses its `write_allowed` at :556. Neither binds the manifest to a pre-dispatch digest. Reproduction: declare only `src/a.py`, have an unconfined worktree worker overwrite the main checkout's run `manifest.yaml` to add `scripts/**`, then create `scripts/pwn.py` in its worktree. The worktree gate cannot see the external manifest write, and both verdicts evaluate the patch against the widened lane.
findings.recommendation: Seal the validated manifest with a pre-dispatch digest stored outside worker reach, and verify that digest before Gate, Record, authority, and Finalize. Refuse any mismatch; do not support unconfined backends until the control plane is isolated.

findings.claim: The enforcement CLIs remain vulnerable to Python module shadowing, including source and legacy `.pyc` files loaded before the new cache controls take effect.
findings.evidence: scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py imports `json`, `subprocess`, and `tempfile` at :54-62 before setting `sys.dont_write_bytecode` at :70; the integration authority does the same at scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py:101-116, and the scope checker at scripts/compound-v-scope-check.py:115-128. Pipeline commands use `-B`, not isolated mode, e.g. scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:3372-3375. In this repository, a direct worker can plant `scripts/yaml.py` whose `safe_load` returns a widened manifest; `_load_yaml` imports it at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:221-229 before deriving the lane. A planted `scripts/json.py` or legacy `scripts/json.pyc` executes even earlier. `-B` prevents writing caches but does not prevent reading or module shadowing.
findings.recommendation: Run all enforcement Python entry points with `-I -B` on the Python 3.9 floor, or explicitly remove the script directory/project cwd from `sys.path` before imports. Add regression tests that plant hostile `yaml.py`, `json.py`, and legacy top-level `.pyc` modules.

findings.claim: The authority verifies a live tree, but Finalize later stages that tree again; post-authority mutation can land unverified bytes and can cause a worktree whose patch never landed to be pruned.
findings.evidence: Finalize runs the authority at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:3371-3384, then performs other writes and only later calls `merge_back` at :3428 and :3476. `merge_back` stages current bytes and creates a fresh patch at :2681-2696 without checking the authority's digest; an empty patch is treated as success at :2689-2690. A single wave commit SHA is then assigned to every merged job at :3521-3526, and every recorded worktree is force-removed at :3578-3599. Reproduction: let two worktree jobs pass authority; after that, revert job B to its baseline while job A remains changed. B's empty patch returns success, A creates the wave commit, and both worktrees are marked integrated and pruned even though B's verified diff is absent from the commit. Altering an approved file instead of reverting it lands bytes the authority never saw.
findings.recommendation: Materialize and digest an immutable per-job binary patch at Gate time. Have the authority validate that artifact, apply exactly it, and prove each job's patch is represented in the resulting commit before pruning its worktree.

findings.claim: Worker-writable `state.json` can forge the idempotence marker and make Finalize skip a real worktree merge permanently.
findings.evidence: Record preserves preexisting fields from the job's state entry at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:3063-3069 and updates rather than replaces them at :3270-3273. Finalize trusts `merged.realised_commit` plus `integrated` and skips `merge_back` at :3461-3465 without Git proof. An unconfined worktree worker can write the main run's state outside its gated tree, set `merged.realised_commit` to its known worktree HEAD and `integrated:true`, then return normally. For an existing-file modification, Finalize finds nothing to commit in the main checkout, reports the idempotent path, leaves the worktree unmerged, and every resume repeats the skip.
findings.recommendation: Treat state as a cache, never authority. On the idempotent branch, prove from Git or a sealed per-job patch digest that the exact worktree diff is already in the recorded commit; otherwise run merge-back again or refuse.

findings.claim: Ordinary test-generated files can turn an honest scope pass into an authority contradiction, despite documentation claiming test byproducts are outside the gate's authority.
findings.evidence: The initial scope check and digest occur at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:2477-2516, then the test floor runs at :2557-2600. The authority later reruns the scope checker at scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py:867-884. That checker deliberately includes ignored files at scripts/compound-v-scope-check.py:201-214. Therefore a job limited to `src/**` whose successful `pytest` creates `.pytest_cache/**`, or whose coverage run creates an ignored artifact, is re-derived as blocked and the receipt becomes `contradicted`. This conflicts with skills/backend-launcher/SKILL.md:299-304, which says such byproducts are outside gate authority and merely excluded from merge staging.
findings.recommendation: Run tests in a disposable copy or capture the immutable job patch before tests and make the authority validate that artifact. Add an end-to-end test where a green floor creates ignored and non-ignored byproducts.

findings.claim: The claimed 'never read an in-tree cache' property disappears when temporary cache-directory creation fails; the code silently proceeds with an unsafe import.
findings.evidence: hooks/lane-guard.sh:269-275 continues without `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` if `mkdir` fails. `_load_module_from_path` similarly catches `mkdtemp` failure and still calls `exec_module` at scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:373-385. The authority repeats this pattern at scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py:653-666. These paths contradict the 'FROM SOURCE—never from a cache beside it' claims and allow a planted unchecked-hash cache to execute when temp storage is unavailable.
findings.recommendation: If a safe cache prefix cannot be established, do not call importlib. The hook should emit an explicit fail-open notice; the authority should fail closed. Test with forced `mkdir`/`mkdtemp` failure plus a planted forged cache.

findings.claim: The lane guard's interpreter-selection paths are not actually bounded and can stall a tool call rather than fail open.
findings.evidence: The viability probes at hooks/lane-guard.sh:352-353 have no watchdog, and the PreToolUse registration has no timeout at hooks/hooks.json:30-38. A candidate wrapper containing `sleep 30` blocks `_cv_can_yaml` before any verdict or failure log. The delegated parser separately allows five seconds and another one-second cleanup at hooks/lane-guard.sh:808-825, despite the header claiming every path is bounded. Logging is also best-effort at :341-346, so an unwritable log makes some fail-open paths silent.
findings.recommendation: Put every probe and delegated parse under a portable sub-second watchdog and add a hook-level timeout. On timeout, emit one valid fail-open notice and stop probing further candidates.

findings.claim: Re-verification after a pruned worktree accepts a commit merely because any touched path matches the job lane; it does not prove that job's patch was merged.
findings.evidence: When the gate root is gone, scripts/compound-v-integration-gate.py:628-690 trusts state plus commit existence/ancestry and computes `in_lane` with `any(...)` at :682-683. Any ancestor commit touching one permitted path satisfies this branch, even if it contains unrelated files or no bytes from this job. This is especially weak for normal wave commits containing several jobs. Reproduction: point a pruned job's state `merged.commit` at any ancestor that touches one allowed file; the branch returns `pass` before verifying its original receipt, diff digest, or per-job patch.
findings.recommendation: Bind each merged job to a per-job patch/tree digest at merge time and verify that binding on resume. Commit existence plus one matching pathname is not adequate evidence.

findings.claim: The run-directory exemption documentation is internally false: it says exactly three files are exempt and that receipts/results are not, while the implementation exempts more.
findings.evidence: scripts/compound-v-emit-workflow.py:2159-2191 describes an 'EXACT, CLOSED LIST' of three files and says receipts/results are not exempt. The tuple at :2198-2220 also exempts `receipts/<id>.gate.json` and `results/<id>.json`, while :2221-2224 adds arbitrarily many archived attempts.
findings.recommendation: Update the docstring and security rationale to enumerate the actual exemption classes, then add one table-driven test generated from the same canonical list.

blind_spots_checked: Partition/glob overlap: the submitted artifact is a claim-and-diff review, not a job manifest with task write scopes, so no task-pair overlap was available to expand.
Shared contract coupling: manifest, state, baseline, receipt, result, and triage-stream ownership were traced across Gate, Record, authority, Finalize, and resume.
Sequencing: checked worker-to-gate, gate-to-tests, tests-to-authority, authority-to-merge, commit-to-prune, and re-finalization paths.
Model routing: checked the new implementer role, Claude agent fallback, Codex isolation, and the documented lower-trust external backends; no separate tier-selection defect was found.
Acceptance: inspected selftests and the real test-floor ordering, including ignored test artifacts and failure-only branches.
Portability: reviewed the changed shell syntax for Bash 3.2 and Python syntax/APIs for the 3.9 floor; no direct incompatibility was found.
Hook guarantees: checked Stop/PreToolUse fail-open behavior, logging, interpreter viability, and timeout bounds.
Bytecode defenses: checked import timing, source/cache lookup paths, temp-directory failure, and module-shadowing channels.
Resume/data loss: checked state idempotence, missing worktrees, merged-commit verification, and per-job versus wave-level prune evidence.
